name.text: Algebra of Sets: Identifying Laws in Set Operations

questiontext.text:
[[ if test='is(question_test=1)' ]]

Which law of sets states that for any set \(A,\)

  • \( A \cap A = A \)
  • \( A \cup A = A \)
[[ elif test='is(question_test=7)']]

Which law of sets states that for any sets \(A, \, B\) and \(C,\)

  • \( A \cap (B \cup C) = (A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C) \)
  • \( A \cup (B \cap C) = (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C) \)
[[ else ]]

Which law of sets states that for any sets \(A\) and \(B,\)

  • \( A \cap B = B \cap A \)
  • \( A \cup B = B \cup A \)
[[/ if]]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

[[ if test='is(question_test=1)' ]]

Idempotent Law:

This law states that for a set \(A\):

  • \( A \cap A = A \)
  • \( A \cup A = A \)

These laws imply that the result of taking the intersection or union of a set with itself is simply the set itself.

[[ elif test='is(question_test=7)']]

Distributive Law:

This law states that for any sets \(A, \, B\) and \(C,\)

  • \( A \cap (B \cup C) = (A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C) \)
  • \( A \cup (B \cap C) = (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C) \)

    • These laws distribute the intersection and union operations over each other.

[[ else ]]

Commutative Law:

This law states that for sets \(A\) and \(B,\)

  • \( A \cap B = B \cap A \)
  • \( A \cup B = B \cup A \)

These laws indicate that the order of sets in the intersection and union operations doesn't matter.

[[/ if]]
